transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

Water collecting under the salad drawers is almost always a blocked defrost drain. The back wall of the fridge frosts up and defrosts on its own every so often. That water runs down a channel into a small hole at the bottom of the back wall, then through a tube to a tray on the motor at the back, where it evaporates. If the hole clogs with bits of food or gunk, the water has nowhere to go and pools in the bottom. That's why it keeps coming back however often you mop. It's normally a simple clean, not a part. 1. Take out the salad drawers and look at the bottom of the back wall for a small hole or slot, often at the end of a groove or channel.
2. Clear it gently with a cotton bud or a soft pipe cleaner. Don't use anything sharp, because there are cooling pipes in the wall.
3. Flush it with warm water, using a turkey baster, syringe or squeezy bottle. If the water drains away freely, it's clear. If it backs up or overflows, it's still blocked, or the tube may be frozen further down.
4. Dry the bottom, refit the drawers and check again tomorrow. If the hole looks clear but water won't go down, the tube is probably frozen lower down. Switching the fridge off for a few hours with towels down, or gently warming the area with warm water, usually frees it. If it drains fine but water still appears, the next things to check are:
• the drip tray and tube at the back near the bottom (switch off and unplug first), to make sure the tube sits in the tray and the tray isn't cracked
• that no food or packaging is pressed against the back wall
• that the door seal isn't split or gapping
• that the fridge isn't leaning forward Let me know what you find with the drain hole.
ok i took the draws out and theres a little groove with a hole at the bottom of the back wall, its got bits of lettuce and gunk in it. il try it with a cotton bud and warm water now

Lettuce and gunk in that hole is very likely the whole story. It's the classic cause of water under the salad drawers, so you're on the right track. A few tips while you do it:
1. Scoop the loose bits out of the groove first, so you don't push them further down the hole.
2. Work the cotton bud or a soft pipe cleaner gently into the hole. Never use anything sharp or stiff, because the cooling pipes run close by.
3. Flush with warm (not boiling) water, a little at a time. Keep a towel in the bottom to catch any overflow.
4. Watch what the water does. If it drains away steadily, the drain is clear and that should be the fix. If it sits or backs up, there's still a clog or ice further down the tube. Keep flushing slowly with warm water, and if that doesn't shift it, switch the fridge off for a few hours with towels down to let any ice thaw. Once it's draining, dry the bottom, refit the drawers and check again over the next day or two. If water still appears even though the hole drains freely, the next suspects are the tube or drip tray at the back, or the door seal. We can look at those then. Let me know whether the water drains away freely or backs up.
ok did it, scooped the lettuce out then cotton bud and warm water. the water went straight down the hole no problem. il keep an eye on it over the next few days

That sounds like it's sorted. 1. Keep loose salad leaves in a bag or box, so bits don't fall down the back of the drawers.
2. Keep food from pressing against the back wall.
3. Every couple of months, give the drain hole a quick flush with warm water from a squeezy bottle or baster. If water does come back over the next few days even though the hole is draining, check the drip tray and tube at the back (switched off and unplugged first). Also check the door seal for splits or gaps. Those are the next most likely causes. Is there anything else I can help with?

candidates: Blocked defrost drain hole at the bottom of the back wall (high)
Drain tube frozen lower down or drip tray/tube out of place at the back (medium)
Excess condensation from a poor door seal, food against the back wall, or the fridge tilting forward (low)
